messages:
devon: Heads-up — saw a p99 jump in prod after yesterday's kernel-selector change, digging in.

maria: Observed on both hosted and dedicated or just hosted? Any numbers?

devon: Hosted mostly. Quick window (12:00-13:00 UTC): p95=120ms, p99=430ms for small payloads (avg tokens ~48). Baseline last week p99 ~220ms.

cheng: Do we have KV cache stats for the window? Could be cache thrash / extra KV fetch latency.

devon: KV hit rate dropped from 0.98 -> 0.91 during spike. Queue latency distro shows much fatter tail vs normal.

lucy: I pulled a profiler from a canary node: kernel selection CPU overhead spiked. We saw a lot of fallbacks to the slower GEMM path for batches assumed to be long (seq_len>1024) even though actual seq_len was ~64 — looks like selector misprediction.

devon: Root cause theory: kernel selector uses conservative upper bound derived from max_batch_tokens. With max_batch_tokens=16384 we aggregated lots of short requests into big token batches; the selector assumed long sequences and picked fallback kernels that have higher setup+per-token cost for short sequences. That increases tail latency.

maria: So microbatch sizing and scheduler params are directly impacting kernel selection heuristics. For latency SLOs we probably want smaller microbatches or different heuristics. Options?

cheng: Short list: 1) lower max_batch_tokens (eg 8192), 2) reduce max_wait_ms from 10 -> 3 for latency-sensitive profile, 3) add adaptive selector that uses observed seq_len distribution instead of worst-case upper bound.

devon: Quick config I tested locally:
```
scheduler:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  max_microbatch_tokens: 512
  max_wait_ms: 3
  latency_priority: true
```

lucy: Replay results with that config: p95=95ms, p99=210ms. Throughput dropped ~8% on the replay, but tail is much tighter.

devon: I also tried keeping max_wait_ms=10 but changing kernel selector to prefer fast kernel when median_seq_len < 256. That gave p99 ~230ms and throughput similar to baseline. So we have a choice: hurt throughput a bit or tweak selector to avoid conservative fallbacks.

maria: What's the safe canary plan? We shouldn't change global defaults without targeting.

devon: Proposal: add two scheduling profiles:
- latency-sensitive: max_wait_ms=3, max_batch_tokens=8192
- throughput (default): max_wait_ms=12, max_batch_tokens=32768
Route customers by SLO tag. Canary: 5% hosted traffic to latency profile for a day, measure p95/p99 and throughput.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary config rolled to 5% on staging at 2026-06-12T15:30 (ref cfg-2026-06-12-01).

lucy: Also add an exposed metric for kernel-selector-fallback-rate (counter) — currently we don't surface it and it's crucial for debugging. I'll add it to the runtime metrics.

cheng: Suggestion: add an alert if KV hit_rate drops >2% sustained for 5m — that would catch cache thrash early and avoid long tails.

maria: Good. devon — can you open the PR + runbook with rollback steps (revert selector change and revert profile routing) before starting canary?

devon: Yep — I'll open PR + runbook now and kick off canary in 30m. If p99 doesn't improve or throughput drops >15% we'll revert.

lucy: Also logging note: add a lightweight per-request tag when we take the fallback kernel so we can trace across traces.

devon: Thanks all. Follow-ups: PR (#2712), runbook, metric PR, alert SR-137. Will post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
